title: Beyond State of Health: Interfacial Degradation, Diagnostic Uncertainty, and Safety-Critical Ageing in Second-Life Lithium-Ion Batteries
content: Second-life lithium-ion batteries are commonly evaluated through state-of-health indi-cators such as residual capacity and internal resistance. However, these metrics do not fully capture the chemical and interfacial ageing processes that determine the safety, reliability, and long-term performance of repurposed batteries. This review critically examines the degradation pathways that are particularly relevant for second-life appli-cations, including solid–electrolyte interphase evolution, cathode–electrolyte interphase instability, electrolyte oxidation and gas generation, lithium plating, transition-metal dissolution, particle cracking, loss of electrical contact, and thermal instability. Special attention is given to the mismatch between apparent electrochemical performance and hidden safety-critical degradation. The review discusses how first-life ageing history influences second-life behavior, why batteries with similar state-of-health values may present different risk profiles, and how advanced diagnostic tools can support safer screening, grading, and repurposing decisions. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, differential voltage analysis, incremental capacity analysis, gas analysis, thermal testing, post-mortem characterization, and operando techniques are evaluated as complementary tools for identifying degradation signatures beyond conventional capacity-based metrics. Finally, a mechanism-informed framework is proposed to connect interfacial degradation, diagnostic uncertainty, battery management strategies, and second-life suitability. This perspective aims to support the development of safer, more reliable, and scientifically grounded pathways for the reuse of lithium-ion batteries in stationary energy storage and circular-economy applications.
